slides.heading: What is a List?
slides.body: What is a List? is part of Lists and Mutable Sequences. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: What is a List?
slides.body: A list stores multiple values in one variable. Lists are useful when a program needs to keep a collection of related items.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: A list is like a shopping basket that can hold several items at the same time.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Lists use square brackets, zero-based indexes, and can be changed after creation.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Create a list of two school supplies and print it.
slides.hint: Put two strings inside square brackets.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Create a list named subjects with Math and Python, then print it.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
